tracking_and_ingestion_systems.cv_pipeline_specs: Dual track: (1) licensed/official event, roster, play-by-play and tracking feeds; (2) an independently operated video path for games where rights permit. Ingest camera streams through an edge GPU (NVDEC/GStreamer), normalize clock and camera calibration, and run a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector (players, ball/puck, officials, goal/posts and field markings) followed by ByteTrack identity association. YOLOv8's official documentation describes its real-time accuracy/speed tradeoff and unified Python API (https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolov8/); ByteTrack associates low-confidence as well as high-confidence boxes to reduce fragmented trajectories and reports 30 FPS on a V100 in its reference implementation (https://github.com/FoundationVision/ByteTrack). Sample/track at 10 Hz (100 ms event-time buckets), interpolate only across bounded occlusions, and emit x/y (and z where stereo/depth is available), velocity, acceleration, heading, confidence, camera_id, calibration_version and track_id. Calibrate homography separately for NFL/MLS fields, MLB diamond, NBA court and NHL rink; fuse views with a Kalman/constant-acceleration filter, Hungarian/ByteTrack association, jersey/OCR embeddings and possession constraints. A Flink keyed stream joins coordinates to official play clocks, debounces duplicate events, flags clock drift and confidence gaps, and publishes immutable raw frames plus corrected feature events to Kafka. Preserve video hash, model weights, annotation/version, source license and quality metrics; never claim CV output is official tracking. Use the NFL Next Gen Stats portal as a reference for tracking-derived concepts such as completion probability, CPOE, EPA and success rate (https://www.nfl.com/next-gen-stats/).

official_feed_integration.value: Use a paid, contract-specific official-data adapter (Sportradar or the applicable league/provider), not website scraping. Its Official Media Data Addendum explicitly identifies NBA Player Tracking Data and MLB Statcast Data as Advanced Statistics and defines Official Data as licensed APIs/feeds for NBA, NHL, MLB and other rights-holder competitions (https://developer.sportradar.com/sportradar-updates/page/official-media-data-addendum).

Implement provider-specific connectors with OAuth/API-key vaulting, rate-limit budgets, retries, idempotency keys, schema mapping, roster/player/venue crosswalks and source timestamps. Sportradar's odds documentation says authentication is required, maps sports/competitions/books/schedules to event markets, and provides a five-minute market-change log (https://developer.sportradar.com/odds/reference/oc-prematch-overview).

Kafka topics: feed.raw.<provider>, feed.normalized.event, pbp.play, tracking.coordinate, odds.quote and correction.*; partition by league/event_id, retain raw payloads, and use a schema registry with backward-compatible Avro/Protobuf. Reconcile official events against CV evidence with a late-data watermark and a quarantine/dead-letter topic.

Provider coverage and state must be explicit: Sportradar's US prematch API documents top US bookmakers and markets spanning NFL, NBA, MLB and soccer (https://developer.sportradar.com/odds/reference/oc-prematch-overview); Caesars' sportsbook page demonstrates jurisdiction-specific legal/non-legal state routes (https://www.caesars.com/sportsbook-and-casino).

commercial_and_legal_framework.derived_data_strategy: Separate raw licensed content, normalized facts, derived features, model parameters, predictions and customer-visible analytics in distinct catalogs. Sell only an approved Derived Data product: aggregates, feature vectors, probabilities, projections, alerts and model explanations that are materially transformed, non-reconstructive and accompanied by source/provenance IDs; prohibit republishing raw PBP/tracking, replaying a live game, or allowing a customer to reverse-engineer the feed. Treat league/team/player marks, NIL/name-image-likeness, footage and proprietary advanced statistics as separately cleared rights. This is a risk-control architecture, not legal advice: the Sportradar addendum says leagues own Official Content, rights are limited/revocable/non-sublicensable/nontransferable and for media/editorial non-commercial use, and expressly bars betting use and new derivative data points without written approval (https://developer.sportradar.com/sportradar-updates/page/official-media-data-addendum). Therefore obtain a commercial/betting/analytics order form and written derived-data and resale permission before launch; maintain a rights matrix per sport, provider, field, latency, territory, customer class and retention period.
commercial_and_legal_framework.sub_licensing_compliance: Make every tenant's entitlement a policy decision: provider_contract_id -> permitted product/field/latency/territory/use -> expiry. Default deny; enforce purpose limitation, no sublicensing, no redistribution, no competitive-product use, no ad-triggering and no live/near-live simulation unless expressly licensed. Sportradar's general terms require customer compliance with applicable laws and licenses/permits, and its license restrictions prohibit making the service available to third parties or exploiting Data/Content outside authorized properties (https://developer.sportradar.com/sportradar-updates/page/terms-and-conditions). Contracts should define whether the platform is a reseller, managed service, or downstream API licensee; flow-down terms, audit rights, takedown/kill switch, deletion on termination, attribution, indemnity, security, SLA, rate limits and regulator/geofencing obligations. Keep a rights ledger and immutable access logs; counsel should review state gambling, exchange, fantasy, advertising, privacy, biometric/video and consumer-protection rules in each jurisdiction.
commercial_and_legal_framework.api_distribution_architecture: Expose REST/GraphQL for historical queries and WebSocket/SSE for licensed live analytics, fronted by an API gateway/WAF with mTLS for enterprise, OAuth2 client credentials, tenant-scoped JWT claims, per-tenant quotas, field-level authorization, jurisdiction/device geofencing, billing meters and provider-rate-limit backpressure. Use a tenant_id row/partition policy, separate encryption keys, logically isolated caches and optional dedicated VPC/private-link deployment. Return product_id, model_version, as_of timestamp, freshness/latency, confidence interval, rights classification, attribution and non-reconstruction limits with each response. An entitlement service checks the rights ledger before query planning; a transformation service reads only approved columns; raw feeds stay in a private bucket. Version and deprecate endpoints with one current/two prior versions, consistent with the API lifecycle described in the provider terms (https://developer.sportradar.com/sportradar-updates/page/terms-and-conditions).

data_lifecycle_2018_2025.historical_pbp_storage: Bronze: immutable 2018-2024 provider payloads in object storage, encrypted and content-addressed; Silver: canonical event_id/game_id/team_id/player_id/play_clock schema with corrections as bitemporal records; Gold: feature tables and model-ready labels. Partition by sport/season/date/league and cluster by game_id; retain source timestamp, ingestion timestamp, correction lineage and license class. Delta Lake is suitable because its documentation specifies ACID/serializable transactions, schema enforcement, batch+stream unification, time travel, upserts/deletes and Spark/Flink connectors (https://docs.delta.io/latest/delta-intro.html). Use Delta Change Data Feed for corrections and reproducible snapshots; compact small files and vacuum only after contractual retention windows.
data_lifecycle_2018_2025.high_res_tracking_lakehouse: For 2025+ (and any earlier games with rights), store raw 10-Hz coordinates as compressed Parquet/Arrow in a high-resolution Bronze zone, with a Silver long table keyed by game_id, period/inning, event_time_ms, entity_id, x/y/z, vx/vy, possession, confidence, source and calibration/model version. Keep a separate video-manifest table (hash, URI, retention and consent/rights status), not unrestricted video in the analytics tables. Use Iceberg for the tracking lakehouse where multi-engine access, hidden partitioning, schema/partition evolution, snapshots and concurrent writers matter: the project documents support for Spark, Flink, Trino, schema evolution, hidden partitions, time travel and serializable atomic commits (https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/). Recommended layout is sport/season/game_date with bucket(game_id) and event-time clustering; roll up 10-Hz raw to play/shift/possession features for ordinary customers while preserving high-res entitlement behind policy.
data_lifecycle_2018_2025.backtesting_framework: Build an as-of feature store and walk-forward evaluator: each training row can see only data whose source_time <= cutoff, with frozen roster/injury/lineup/odds snapshots and a feature/model/rights manifest. Split chronologically by season (train 2018-2021, tune 2022, validate 2023, blind test 2024; separately evaluate 2025+ tracking), and run expanding-window retraining plus event-level leakage tests. Simulate quote availability, closing-line movement, latency, voids, scratches, limits, vig, exchange fees and bankroll; report calibration/Brier/log loss, AUC, MAE/RMSE, CRPS, cover/ROI, CLV, max drawdown, turnover and confidence intervals. Delta time travel or Iceberg snapshots make the exact dataset reproducible (https://docs.delta.io/latest/delta-intro.html; https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/). Store every prediction, decision, price, available timestamp and eventual settlement; compare champion/challenger models and use pre-registered thresholds rather than cherry-picked windows.

dfs_and_prop_modeling.prop_correlation_logic: Represent a game as a joint generative model, not independent player projections. For each sport, simulate latent pace/possessions, team scoring, lineup/minutes or plate appearances, then conditional player opportunity and conversion. Use a covariance/copula or multivariate Bayesian model with team/game random effects and context factors. Examples: NBA minutes and usage jointly drive points/assists/rebounds; NFL pass attempts, targets, receptions, yards and touchdowns share drive/game-script factors; MLB plate appearances, balls-in-play and pitcher/batter handedness drive hits/HR/RBI; NHL shots, power-play time and goals share skater/goalie/game state; soccer minutes, shots, xG, assists and cards share possession, formation and score state. For a parlay or correlated prop set A, compute P(A) from the same Monte Carlo draws (and P(X>line,Y>line), not P(X>line)P(Y>line)); estimate sensitivity to shared latent variables, shrink unstable correlations, and stress-test lineup/pace scenarios. Preserve push/void rules and book-specific settlement semantics.
dfs_and_prop_modeling.dfs_optimization_strategies: For salary DFS, solve a mixed-integer program: maximize E[fantasy_points] + lambda*leverage - risk_penalty, subject to salary cap, roster/position, team/game limits and late-swap; add covariance-aware variance/CVaR and ownership fade/stack constraints. Generate thousands of lineups by randomized projections, late news re-optimization and exposure caps. For PrizePicks/Underdog Pick'em-style higher/lower entries, treat each leg as a threshold event; price leg probability from the joint simulation, calculate payout-specific expected value, and select entries only after accounting for platform rules, correlation, ties/pushes, entry limits and any stated payout table. Underdog's help page distinguishes Pick'em higher/lower player props from Prediction Picks, where contracts are probability-priced and settle $1/$0 (https://help.underdogsports.com/en/articles/14127507-what-are-prediction-picks); do not conflate those products. For LineStar-style workflows, provide projection/prop-edge, ownership, salary comparison, confirmed lineups, live scoring and update audit—features its site publicly enumerates (https://www.linestarapp.com/). Never automate account wagering or imply guaranteed wins; make jurisdiction and responsible-play controls first-class.
dfs_and_prop_modeling.injury_impact_variables: Use a hierarchical injury/availability state: status probability, expected minutes/snaps/plate appearances/TOI, return-to-play ramp, re-injury risk, position replacement quality, teammate usage redistribution, defensive matchup, pace, foul/trouble risk, travel/rest, weather/roof/ice and coach rotation. Ingest timestamped reports and confirmation/starting-lineup signals; model missing-not-at-random reporting and create scenario weights (active, limited, out). Recompute on news with an event-time feature view, not overwriting history. For tracking, quantify pre/post injury speed, acceleration, route separation, workload and shift length only when rights and medical/privacy policies allow. Prop impact is the difference between scenario distributions: Delta P = P(prop|injury scenario)-P(prop|baseline), with uncertainty intervals and a minimum edge threshold.

market_intelligence_and_edge.real_time_scraping_architecture: Prefer licensed odds APIs/official partnerships; scrape public pages only where terms, robots, authorization and rate limits permit. Use one adapter per FanDuel, Caesars, BetUS and other approved source with isolated egress, browser/API protocol, bookmaker-specific parsers, schema tests, circuit breakers, exponential backoff and no CAPTCHA/security bypass. Normalize event/participant/market/period/line/selection/price/limits/status/last_updated into an odds quote; map aliases via a versioned crosswalk and retain raw HTML/JSON hash plus source timestamp. Kafka ingests quote events; Flink deduplicates, validates monotonic timestamps, detects stale/suspended/obvious-error prices, joins schedule/roster state and maintains an in-memory best-price/order-book view; sink raw and normalized history to Delta/Iceberg. Sportradar's Odds Comparison documentation provides the safer reference architecture: authenticated feeds, books/sports/competitions/schedules, event-market endpoints and a five-minute change log (https://developer.sportradar.com/odds/reference/oc-prematch-overview). Action Network and Vegas Insider demonstrate public odds/picks/market-analysis product patterns (https://www.actionnetwork.com/; https://www.vegasinsider.com/), while BetUS publicly exposes odds, props builder and same-game-parlay categories (https://www.betus.com.pa/sportsbook/). Respect each operator's terms, do not place bets, and apply jurisdictional display restrictions.
market_intelligence_and_edge.edge_detection_algorithms: Convert American odds: for positive a, p_raw=100/(a+100); for negative a, p_raw=|a|/(|a|+100). For a mutually exclusive market, remove vig by p_i=p_raw_i/sum(p_raw); for two-sided markets use a proportional or Shin-style de-vig model and retain uncertainty. Model fair probability p_hat with a calibrated ensemble: sport-specific Poisson/negative-binomial score or goal model (MLB/NHL/soccer), possession/drive simulation (NBA/NFL), Bayesian state-space ratings, and Glicko-2/Elo priors with venue, rest, lineup and weather covariates. PyMC is appropriate for Bayesian comparison/modeling workflows (https://www.pymc.io/projects/docs/en/stable/learn.html), and Stan supports Bayesian linear, multilevel and time-series models (https://mc-stan.org/). Generate 50k-500k common-random-number Monte Carlo paths for player props, totals and correlated parlays; calculate EV for a $1 stake as EV=p_hat*net_win-(1-p_hat)*stake-fees, edge=p_hat-p_market, and CLV against a timestamped closing line. Bet only when lower confidence bound on EV exceeds a sport/market/latency threshold after model error, limits, slippage, taxes and exchange fees; rank by fractional Kelly f*=edge/odds and cap it (e.g., 0.1 Kelly) with portfolio covariance and max-drawdown constraints. Calibrate with isotonic/beta calibration, monitor Brier/log loss, reliability curves, drift, stale-feed rate and closing-line performance; publish uncertainty and abstain when feed/model disagreement is high. BettingPros visibly uses EV and cover-probability language, a useful product precedent but not evidence of future performance (https://www.bettingpros.com/).

tech_stack: Cloud object storage (S3/ADLS/GCS) + Parquet/Arrow; Delta Lake for transactional Spark-centric PBP/features and Apache Iceberg for high-resolution multi-engine tables; Apache Kafka/Schema Registry for durable event streams and Apache Flink for low-latency keyed joins, windows, state and corrections (Kafka describes durable publish/subscribe, replay, partitions, replication and exactly-once processing at https://kafka.apache.org/intro; Flink project/docs at https://flink.apache.org/what-is-flink/); Apache Spark SQL/Structured Streaming/MLlib for batch, feature engineering and distributed simulation; Python with PyTorch/Ultralytics YOLOv8, ByteTrack, NumPy, Polars and scikit-learn; PyMC and Stan for hierarchical Bayesian inference; Ray/Dask or Spark for Monte Carlo; OR-Tools/Gurobi for lineup optimization; Postgres for metadata/rights/billing, Redis for hot odds/projection cache, ClickHouse/Trino for low-latency analytics, and Kubernetes with GPU node pools for CV/model serving. Use MLflow/model registry, Great Expectations/Deequ, OpenTelemetry/Prometheus/Grafana, Vault/KMS, IAM/RBAC/ABAC, Terraform and GitHub Actions. Architecture principles: immutable raw evidence, bitemporal corrections, reproducible snapshots, contract tests, canary/champion models, tenant isolation, auditability and an explicit rights-policy enforcement point before every data read or API response.
